source.title: Parabolicity conjecture of F-isocrystals

The Annals article (received 13 February 2021, revised 7 January 2023, accepted 6 February 2023, online 31 August 2023) is not freely served; v4 postdates acceptance. Item locators are v4's pages; every recorded mistake was checked on a page image.

sourceVersions.note: arXiv v4, 8 February 2023, "final version, to appear in Annals of Mathematics", posted two days after acceptance. The published article, Ann. of Math. 198 (2023), 619–656, doi:10.4007/annals.2023.198.2.3, is not freely served and was not read, so every finding is scoped to v4.

summary: D'Addezio proves Crew's parabolicity conjecture: for an overconvergent F-isocrystal M† with constant slopes on a smooth variety over a perfect field, the monodromy group of the underlying convergent isocrystal is the stabiliser in G(M†, η) of the slope filtration, hence parabolic when M† is semisimple. The key input is the minimal-slope property of †-hulls (Theorem 4.1.3): the smallest overconvergent subobject containing N has the same minimal-slope part as N. It is proved for curves at the generic point with de Jong's reverse slope filtration, and in higher dimension through a new Lefschetz theorem for docile overconvergent F-isocrystals, whose proof uses the curve case and monodromy groups of isocrystals with a punctual Q_p^ur-lattice. Applications: semisimplicity of Gr^S R^1f_crys for abelian schemes over finite fields, finiteness of separable p-power torsion, Kedlaya's conjecture, strong multiplicity one by minimal-slope Hecke eigenvalues (with Abe's correspondence), and the PBS filtration. The cited foundations are missing and routed as a source of PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology (RD.1–RD.3 and RD.5); the curve case coalesces with PAPER-TSUZUKI-23's minimal-slope Part II, and the monodromy theory becomes a new Part II. Fourteen mistakes are recorded after review, all confirmed: a gap in the proof of Proposition 4.2.12 (E5; the theorem it serves is independently in Tsuzuki), an error in the statement of Lemma 4.4.7 that affects nothing (E13), and twelve misprints.

items.name: Convergent and overconvergent isocrystals with Frobenius structure
items.statement: For X smooth over a perfect field k of characteristic p, Isoc(X) = Crys(X)[1/p] (crystals of coherent O_{X,crys}-modules up to isogeny) and Isoc†(X) the overconvergent isocrystals over X/K(k); an F^n-structure is an isomorphism (F^n)*M ≅ M, giving F^n-Isoc(X) and F^n-Isoc†(X), and F^∞-Isoc(X) := 2-colim_n F^n-Isoc(X). F^n-Isoc(X) is equivalent to convergent F^n-isocrystals.
items.note: RD.3 plans overconvergent isocrystals with Frobenius pullback isomorphisms and their restriction to convergent isocrystals. The crystalline description Isoc(X) = Crys(X)[1/p], with its equivalence to convergent F^n-isocrystals ([Ked22, Thm. 2.2]), is not named there, and the 2-colimit F^∞-Isoc(X) is this paper's construction (review).

items.name: Full faithfulness of overconvergent-to-convergent restriction (Kedlaya)
items.statement: The restriction functor α : Isoc†(X)_F → Isoc(X)_F on isocrystals admitting some Frobenius structure is fully faithful; M ∈ Isoc(X)_F is †-extendable if it lies in the essential image, with †-extension M† unique up to isomorphism ([Ked07], [DE22, Cor. 5.7]).
items.note: RD.3 states full faithfulness 'only in the proven source range'; PAPER-TSUZUKI-23/099 marks the same theorem planned there.

items.name: Dieudonné–Manin classification
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed perfect field, an F-isocrystal is, after passing to a power of Frobenius, a direct sum of rank-one objects (K(Ω), p^sσ), s ∈ Z.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.1.5, p. 8; Lemma 4.2.7, p. 15 (arXiv v4)
items.note: Mathlib has the rank-one classification; the general classification is VB0's.

items.name: (φ, ∇)-modules over E, E† and the generic point
items.statement: O_E = (W[t]_{(p)})^∧, O_{E†} ⊂ O_E the series converging on some annulus ∗ ≤ |t| < 1, with Frobenius lift φ(t) = t^p and derivation ∂_t; a (φ, ∇)-module over E or E† is a finite-dimensional space with a φ-linear isomorphism and a connection with ∇∘φ = pt^{p−1}φ∘∇. F-Isoc(k(t)) and F-Isoc†(k(t)) are the (φ, ∇)-modules over E and E†; over K⟨u⟩ and K⟨u⟩† they are F-Isoc(A^1_k) and F-Isoc†(A^1_k).

items.name: Tannaka groups of the subcategory spanned by an object
items.statement: For an object A of a Tannakian category, ⟨A⟩ is the Tannakian subcategory it spans (closed under subobjects) and G(A, ω) the Tannaka group of ⟨A⟩ for a fibre functor ω; H^0(A) = Hom(1, A); the socle and socle filtration of A.
items.note: MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.6 plans Tannaka groups "for each proven neutral Tannakian category". The paper's groups G(M, η) use the fibre functor ω_η with values in K(Ω), which is larger than K(k) unless η is k-rational, so they need Deligne's theory of fibre functors over an extension (Catégories tannakiennes, 1990), which no layer mentions; item 33 (route 6) carries that case (review).

items.name: Parabolic subgroups of reductive groups
items.statement: A parabolic subgroup of a connected reductive group is connected ([Bor91, Thm. 11.16]) and contains a maximal torus; the centraliser of a torus in a connected reductive group is reductive ([Bor91, Cor. 11.12]); a normal subgroup of a reductive group that meets a maximal torus trivially is finite; a finite normal subgroup of a connected group is central, and the centre of a connected reductive group lies in every maximal torus.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 4.3.4–4.3.5, p. 19; Theorem 5.1.6, p. 25 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Weil's Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties
items.statement: Frobenius eigenvalues on H^1 of an abelian variety over a finite field are Weil numbers of weight 1, and so are the eigenvalues of the crystalline Frobenius, which has the same characteristic polynomial. Hence the overconvergent F-isocrystal R^1f_{crys*}O_{A,crys} of an abelian scheme over a variety over a finite field is pure of weight 1.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorems 5.1.6 and 5.2.2, pp. 25–26 (arXiv v4)
items.note: R34.2 imports DWP.1's Weil bound for abelian varieties on the Tate realization. RD.7 plans the comparison of the crystalline and ℓ-adic characteristic polynomials of Frobenius for smooth proper varieties over finite fields, which transfers it to the crystalline Frobenius the paper uses (review).

items.name: Slope filtration after removing a divisor
items.statement: After removing a divisor of X, an F^n-isocrystal has constant slopes and acquires the slope filtration 0 = S_0 ⊊ S_1 ⊊ ··· ⊊ S_m = M with S_i/S_{i−1} isoclinic of slope s_i and s_1 < ··· < s_m ([Kat79, Cor. 2.3.1, 2.6.2], [dO99, Thm. 4.1], [Ked22, Thm. 3.12, Cor. 4.2]).

items.name: Theorem 4.1.6 (Kedlaya): restriction to a dense open
items.statement: For U ⊆ X dense open: (i) F-Isoc(X) → F-Isoc(U) is fully faithful; (ii) F-Isoc†(X) → F-Isoc†(U) is fully faithful and closed under subquotients ([Ked07, Thm. 5.2.1, Prop. 5.3.1], [Ked08, Thm. 4.2.1], [DK17, Thm. 2.2.3]).

items.name: Generic full faithfulness and freeness (Kedlaya)
items.statement: F-Isoc†(k(t)) → F-Isoc(k(t)) is fully faithful ([Ked04, Thm. 5.1]); (φ, ∇)-modules over K⟨u⟩ and K⟨u⟩† are free ([Ked04, Prop. 6.6, Thm. 6.7]); and E ⊗_{E†} E†_alg → E_alg is injective ([Ked04, Prop. 4.1]).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.6 (de Jong): reverse slope filtration
items.statement: A φ-module M†_alg over E†_alg has a reverse slope filtration 0 = S^rev_0 ⊊ ··· ⊊ S^rev_m = M†_alg with (S^rev_i/S^rev_{i−1}) ⊗ E_alg ≅ S_{m+1−i}(M_alg)/S_{m−i}(M_alg) (corrected index, see E3); if M†_alg is isoclinic of slope s/r then, after scaling s and r, M†_alg[p^{1/r}] has a basis with φ(v_i) = p^{s/r}v_i ([deJ98, Prop. 5.5], extended to O†_{E_alg}).

items.name: Unit-root F-isocrystals and p-adic lisse sheaves (Crew)
items.statement: For every n there is a fully faithful Q_{p^n}-linear ⊗-functor LS(X, Q_{p^n}) → F^n-Isoc(X) with essential image the unit-root F^n-isocrystals ([Cre87, Thm. 2.1]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.3.4, p. 11; Theorem 5.3.3, p. 27 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Docile overconvergent isocrystals
items.statement: For X = Y ∖ D with Y smooth proper and D a simple normal crossing divisor, an overconvergent isocrystal is docile if it has unipotent monodromy along D ([Ked07, Def. 4.4.2]); docile objects are stable under sums, tensor products, duals and subquotients ([Ked07, Prop. 3.2.20]), and rank-one docile objects have zero residues, hence are unramified.
items.locator: Definition 4.4.1, p. 19; proof of Corollary 4.4.8, p. 22 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Semistable reduction for overconvergent F-isocrystals (Kedlaya)
items.statement: After a generically finite étale alteration, an overconvergent F-isocrystal becomes docile along a simple normal crossing boundary of a smooth compactification ([Ked11, Thm. 2.4.4]).

items.name: R^1f_crys of an abelian scheme is overconvergent (Étesse)
items.statement: For an abelian scheme f : A → X over a smooth variety over a finite field, R^1f_{crys*}O_{A,crys} is †-extendable ([Ete02, Thm. 7]).

items.name: Crystalline Dieudonné module of A[p^∞] (Berthelot–Breen–Messing)
items.statement: For an abelian scheme A → X, R^1f_{crys*}O_{A,crys} is the crystalline Dieudonné module of A[p^∞] ([BBM82, Thm. 2.5.6(ii)]), and its unit-root part is the Dieudonné module of the étale quotient A[p^∞]^ét.

items.name: Homomorphisms of Barsotti–Tate groups (de Jong)
items.statement: Over a finitely generated field E of characteristic p, End(A) ⊗ Z_p → End of the Dieudonné crystal of A[p^∞] is an isomorphism, so an idempotent of End(M†, Φ†) gives one of End(A) ⊗ Q_p ([deJ98, Thm. 2.6]).

items.name: Chebotarev density for a smooth curve over F_q
items.statement: For a smooth connected curve X over F_q, the Frobenius elements at the closed points outside any finite set are dense in π_1^ét(X); hence a semisimple continuous representation of π_1^ét(X) over a field of characteristic 0 is determined by its Frobenius characteristic polynomials at all but finitely many closed points. The paper cites Serre's general form for schemes of finite type over Z ([Ser66, Thm. 7]) but uses only this case.
items.note: Review: restated for the only case the paper uses (the proof of Theorem 5.3.3, a curve over a finite field). FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 plans a function-field Chebotarev statement for finite Galois covers; the profinite form and the determination of a semisimple representation by its characteristic polynomials follow from it, so the item is a source of FA.5 (route 3).

items.name: Langlands correspondence for isocrystals (Abe)
items.statement: For a curve X over F_q, every Q̄_p-linear cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_r(A) corresponds to an irreducible Q̄_p-linear overconvergent F-isocrystal on a dense open of X with matching Frobenius and Hecke eigenvalues ([Abe18]).

items.name: †-hull of a sub-F^n-isocrystal
items.statement: For an inclusion (N, Φ_N) ⊆ (M, Φ_M) of F^n-isocrystals with M †-extendable, the †-hull N̄ is the smallest †-extendable sub-F^n-isocrystal of M containing N. It exists because †-extendable subobjects of M are closed under finite intersections (the restriction functor α from overconvergent to convergent isocrystals is exact and fully faithful), and because the category of isocrystals is artinian: a subobject of the same rank is the whole object (footnote 6).

items.name: The minimal-slope property MS
items.statement: For †-extendable (M, Φ_M) with constant slopes, MS(M, Φ_M) says S_1(N) = S_1(N̄) for every sub-F^n-isocrystal N ⊆ M; MS(X) says MS(M, Φ_M) holds for every n > 0 and every †-extendable F^n-isocrystal over X with constant slopes.

items.name: Lemmas 4.1.4–4.1.8: reductions for MS
items.statement: To prove MS(X) one may take n = 1 (4.1.4) and check isoclinic sub-F-isocrystals only (4.1.5); MS(M|_U) implies MS(M) for U ⊆ X dense open, since †-hulls commute with restriction (4.1.7); for a finite étale Galois cover f : Y → X, MS(f*M) implies MS(M) and MS(f_*M) implies MS(M) (4.1.8).

items.name: Proposition 4.2.2 (Kedlaya, Tsuzuki): MS at the generic point
items.statement: If N ⊆ M is an inclusion of (φ, ∇)-modules over E and M is †-extendable, then S_1(N) = S_1(N̄).

items.name: Construction 4.2.3 and Lemma 4.2.4: the †-hull by duality
items.statement: With Q† the image of (M†)^∨ → N^∨, one has N ⊆ Q^∨ ⊆ M, and Q^∨ is the †-hull of N in M: the unique submodule containing N and coming from some N̄† ⊆ M† with (N̄†)^∨ → N^∨ injective.

items.name: Rings O_{E_alg}, O†_{E_alg} and their fraction fields
items.statement: O_{E_alg} = W(k(t)^alg), with elements Σ [f_i]p^i; O†_{E_alg} ⊆ O_{E_alg} the series whose t-adic valuations of f_i are bounded below by a linear function of i, Frobenius-stable; E†_alg and E_alg their fraction fields (inside de Jong's Γ_{2,c} and Γ_2).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.7: maps to isoclinic modules
items.statement: If M† is a φ-module over E†, N an isoclinic φ-module over E of slope s/r and ψ : M → N a morphism whose restriction to M† is injective, then the maximal slope of M is s/r and rk(S_m(M)/S_{m−1}(M)) ≤ rk(N).

items.name: Integral models A_n, B_n, B̃_n of overconvergent rings
items.statement: A_n is the image of W⟨u_1, …, u_n⟩ → W⟨u⟩, u_i ↦ ū_i := pu^i; B_n ⊆ O_E is the image of (A_n[t])_{m_n} with m_n = (p, t, ū_1, …, ū_n), also written (A_n[t]/(ū_1t − p, …, ū_nt^n − p))_{m_n}; B′_n = A_n[t]/(ū_1t − p) and B̃_n = (B′_n)_{m_n}, with a surjection B̃_n ↠ B_n whose kernel is killed by p^{n−1}; colim A_n[1/p] = K⟨u⟩† and colim (B_n)^∧[1/p] = colim (B̃_n)^∧[1/p] = E†.

items.name: Lemmas 4.2.10–4.2.11
items.statement: (W⟨u⟩ ⊗̂_{A_n} B̃_n)^∧[1/p] → E is injective (4.2.10); if the p^∞-torsion of an A_n-module M is killed by p^s, so is Tor_1^{A_n}(B′_n, M) (4.2.11).

items.name: Proposition 4.2.12: †-hulls commute with passing to the generic point
items.statement: If N ⊆ M are (φ, ∇)-modules over K⟨u⟩ with M †-extendable and of constant slopes, then N̄ ⊗ E is the †-hull of N ⊗ E in M ⊗ E.
items.note: The printed proof has a gap (E5): the bound p^{−s_n} on which it rests need not exist. Theorem 4.2.13, the proposition's only use, is proved independently by Tsuzuki [Tsu23, Prop. 6.1]; the proposition itself needs a repaired proof.

items.name: Étale covers of the affine line (Kedlaya)
items.statement: Every smooth curve over a perfect field of characteristic p has a dense open admitting a finite étale morphism to A^1_k ([Ked05, Thm. 1]).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.13: MS for curves
items.statement: A smooth curve X over a perfect field k satisfies MS(X) (also [Tsu23, Prop. 6.1]).

items.name: Theorem 4.4.2 (Abe–Esnault): Lefschetz full faithfulness for docile isocrystals
items.statement: If Y ⊆ P^d_k is smooth connected projective of dimension ≥ 2, D a simple normal crossing divisor, and C ⊆ Y a smooth curve which is a complete intersection of hypersurfaces meeting D transversally, then Isoc†(Y ∖ D)^doc → Isoc†(C ∖ D)^doc is fully faithful ([AE19, Cor. 2.4]).

items.name: Crew's monodromy groups G(M, η) and G(M†, η)
items.statement: For X connected and η a perfect point with fibre functor ω_η, G(M, η) is the Tannaka group of ⟨M⟩ ⊆ Isoc(X) and G(M†, η) that of ⟨M†⟩ ⊆ Isoc†(X). For convergent M the former is Crew's DGal(M, η), and the latter is Crew's DGal(M†, η). For an overconvergent F^n-isocrystal M† with underlying F^n-isocrystal M, G(M, η) ⊆ G(M†, η) ⊆ GL(M_η).

items.name: Observable functors and scalar extension of Tannakian categories
items.statement: An exact functor Ψ : C → D of Tannakian categories is observable iff every subquotient of an object in its essential image embeds into an object of the essential image ([DE22, Prop. A.3]); the criteria of [DE22, §A] for closed immersions, faithful flatness and exactness ([DE22, Prop. A.13]) of the induced maps of Tannaka groups; scalar extension of K-linear Tannakian categories along L/K ([Del89, §4.4], [Sta08, Thm. 3.1.3]); and K/F-full faithfulness of a functor from an F-linear to a K-linear Tannakian category ([Sta08, Def. 1.1.2]) with the comparison theorem [Sta08, Thm. 2.4.1], which Lemma 3.3.1 and Proposition 3.3.2 use.

items.name: Isocrystals with punctual Q_p^ur-structure
items.statement: Assuming F̄_p ⊆ k, for a geometric point η of X an isocrystal with Q_p^ur-structure is (M, V_M) with V_M ⊆ ω_η(M) a Q_p^ur-lattice (V_M ⊗ K(Ω) = ω_η(M)); morphisms respect the lattices; this gives Isoc_{Q_p^ur}(X, η).

items.name: Lemma 3.1.3: isocrystals with Q_p^ur-structure form a neutral Tannakian category
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 3.1.1, if X is geometrically connected, Isoc_{Q_p^ur}(X, η) is a Q_p^ur-linear neutral Tannakian category with unit (O_{X/K}, Q_p^ur), dual lattice V_{M^∨} = {f ∈ ω_η(M)^∨ : f(V_M) ⊆ Q_p^ur} and fibre functor (M, V_M) ↦ V_M.

items.name: Dieudonné–Manin Q_p^ur-structure and the functor Λ_η
items.statement: For an F^n-isocrystal (M, Φ_M) over an algebraically closed field Ω, the Q_p^ur-span ω_{Q_p^ur}(M, Φ_M) of the vectors v with Φ^i_M v = p^j v for some (i, j) ∈ Z_{>0} × Z is a Q_p^ur-lattice of M (Lemma 3.1.5); this gives a fibre functor ω_{η,Q_p^ur} on F^∞-Isoc(X) and Λ_η : F^∞-Isoc(X) → Isoc_{Q_p^ur}(X, η), whose essential image consists of the isocrystals with Dieudonné–Manin Q_p^ur-structure.

items.name: Lemmas 3.2.1–3.2.3: trivial subobjects, uniqueness and socles
items.statement: The maximal trivial subobject of an F^n-isocrystal is Φ-stable, so H^0(M, V_M) ⊗_{Q_p^ur} K ≅ H^0(M) for the induced Dieudonné–Manin structure (3.2.1). A semisimple isocrystal has at most one Dieudonné–Manin Q_p^ur-structure up to isomorphism, and with it decomposes as ⊕_i (M_i, V_{M_i})^{⊕a_i} with the M_i irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic (3.2.2). The socle of an isocrystal with Dieudonné–Manin structure inherits one as a subobject, and (M, V_M) semisimple implies M semisimple (3.2.3).

items.name: Propositions 3.2.4–3.2.5: subquotients and observability of Λ_η
items.statement: Each irreducible subquotient of an isocrystal with Dieudonné–Manin Q_p^ur-structure inherits one (3.2.4); Λ_η is observable, and fully faithful on unit-root objects when k = k^alg (3.2.5); the same holds for overconvergent objects.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.8: homotopy exact sequences of monodromy groups
items.statement: For a †-extendable F^n-isocrystal there is a commutative diagram with exact rows 1 → G(M, V_M, η) → G(M, Φ^∞_M, η) → G(M, Φ^∞_M, η)^cst → 1 and its overconvergent analogue; the first two vertical maps are closed embeddings and the last is faithfully flat. Remark 3.2.9 asserts, citing Theorem 4.1.3 and Proposition 4.3.5 and without proof, that the last map is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Definition 3.2.7, Proposition 3.2.8 and Remark 3.2.9, pp. 9–10 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Lemma 3.3.1 and Proposition 3.3.2: base change of monodromy groups
items.statement: With Isoc_{Q_p^ur}(X, η)_F the Tannakian subcategory spanned by the image of Λ_η (Definition 3.2.6), Isoc_{Q_p^ur}(X, η)_F → Isoc(X) is K/Q_p^ur-fully faithful and preserves semisimplicity, and Isoc_{Q_p^ur}(X, η)_F ⊗_{Q_p^ur} K → Isoc(X)_F is an equivalence; so G(M, η) ≅ G(M, V_M, η) ⊗_{Q_p^ur} K.
items.locator: Definition 3.2.6, p. 9; Lemma 3.3.1 and Proposition 3.3.2, pp. 10–11 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Proposition 3.3.4 and Corollary 3.3.6: étale isocrystals and lisse sheaves
items.statement: If k = k^alg, LS(X, Q_p^ur) is equivalent to the category of étale isocrystals with Q_p^ur-structure (Definition 3.3.3, Proposition 3.3.4), and F^∞-Isoc^ét(X) to Q-graded lisse Q_p^ur-sheaves (Remark 3.3.5). For an F^n-isocrystal (M, Φ_M) admitting the slope filtration, an étale path from η to η′ induces isomorphisms G(M, Φ^∞_M, η) ≅ G(M, Φ^∞_M, η′) and G(M, V_M, η) ≅ G(M, V_M, η′) (Corollary 3.3.6).

items.name: Chevalley's theorem
items.statement: Let G be an affine algebraic group over a field and H ⊆ G a closed subgroup. Then there are a finite-dimensional representation V of G and a line L ⊆ V such that H is the stabiliser of L in G.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 4.3.2 and 5.1.4, pp. 18, 25 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Parabolics from filtrations (Saavedra)
items.statement: An exact ⊗-filtration of a fibre functor indexed by (1/r)Z defines a quasi-cocharacter λ : G_m^{1/∞} → G, and for reductive G the subgroup P_G(λ) of ⊗-automorphisms preserving the filtration is parabolic ([Saa72, §2.1, Prop. 2.2.5]).

items.name: The slope quasi-cocharacter λ and P_G(λ)
items.statement: For (M†, Φ†_M) with constant slopes, r the lcm of the slope denominators, the subspaces of slope ≤ s/r of ω_{η,Q_p^ur} form an exact ⊗-filtration S̃_•; it defines λ : G_m^{1/∞} ↠ G_m^{1/r} → G = G(M†, Φ^{†,∞}_M, η), and P_G(λ) is its stabiliser.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.2: MS implies parabolicity for F^∞-monodromy
items.statement: Assume Hypothesis 3.1.1 (an inclusion F̄_p ⊆ k), let η ∈ X(Ω) be a perfect point, (M†, Φ†_M) an overconvergent F^n-isocrystal with constant slopes, G := G(M†, Φ^{†,∞}_M, η) and H := G(M, Φ^∞_M, η). If MS(X) holds, then H = P_G(λ); in particular, if G is reductive then H is a parabolic subgroup of G.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.4: component groups agree
items.statement: If every dense open of X satisfies MS, then π_0(G(M, Φ^∞_M, η)) = π_0(G(M†, Φ^{†,∞}_M, η)) canonically.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.5: †-extendable rank-one objects are overconvergently generated
items.statement: Under §4.3.3, if (L, Φ^∞_L) ∈ ⟨M, Φ^∞_M⟩ is a †-extendable rank-one F^∞-isocrystal then (L†, Φ^{†,∞}_L) ∈ ⟨M†, Φ^{†,∞}_M⟩.

items.name: Corollary 4.3.6
Lemma 4.4.5 (Pink, Serre): curves preserving the monodromy of a lisse sheaf
items.statement: For a lisse Q_p-sheaf V on smooth connected X there is a connected finite Galois étale cover X̃ → X such that for every smooth connected curve C ⊆ X with X̃ ×_X C connected, ⟨V⟩ → ⟨V|_C⟩ is an equivalence (via a finite quotient detecting surjectivity, [Ser89, §10.6], [Kat90, 8.18.3]).

items.name: Lemmas 4.4.6–4.4.7: curves preserving ramification of rank-one objects
items.statement: (4.4.6) For X smooth connected, D ⊆ X an irreducible divisor and V a lisse Q_p-sheaf on X ∖ D, there are a dense smooth open D′ ⊆ D and a conic closed Z ⊆ TX ×_X D′ of codimension 1 in every fibre such that, for every smooth curve C ⊆ X not contained in D and meeting D′ at a closed point x with T_xC ⊄ Z_x, every rank-one L ∈ ⟨V⟩ ramified along D has L|_C ramified at x (a variant of [Dri12, Lem. 5.1]). (4.4.7, corrected) Let Π be a commutative profinite group containing a topologically finitely generated open pro-p subgroup, H ⊆ Π a closed subgroup and n ≥ 1 with (H ∩ p^nΠ) ⊆ pH. For every quotient H ↠ G with G cyclic of prime order (the proof covers G of order prime to p or of order p) there are a morphism Π → Π_tors × Π/p^nΠ and an embedding G ↪ Π_tors × Π/p^nΠ making the square with H ⊆ Π commute. The printed lemma claims this for every cyclic G, which fails for G = Z/p² (E13).

items.name: Corollary 4.4.8: characters of docile monodromy
items.statement: For X as in §4.3.3 with a smooth compactification by a simple normal crossing divisor and (M†, Φ†_M) docile, the characters of G(M†, V†_M) are the unramified characters of G(M, V_M).

items.name: Theorem 4.4.9: Bertini with tangency conditions
items.statement: For Y ⊆ P^d_{k^alg} smooth connected projective of dimension ≥ 2, D a divisor, D′ ⊆ D open, Z ⊆ TY ×_Y D′ conic closed of codimension 1 in each fibre, U ⊆ Y dense open and Ũ → U connected finite étale, there is a smooth complete-intersection curve C meeting D transversally, with C ×_U Ũ connected and non-empty, meeting each component D′_i with tangent directions not all in Z (via Jouanolou [Jou83, Thm. 6.3]).

items.name: Theorem 4.4.3 (Theorem 1.3.1): Lefschetz theorem for docile overconvergent F^n-isocrystals
items.statement: If Y ⊆ P^d_{k^alg} is smooth connected projective of dimension ≥ 2, D a simple normal crossing divisor and (M†, Φ†_M) an overconvergent F^n-isocrystal on X := Y ∖ D docile along D, there is a smooth connected curve C ⊆ X meeting the open where the slopes are constant such that ⟨M†⟩ → ⟨M†|_C⟩ is an equivalence of categories.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.3 (Theorem 1.2.2): minimal slopes of †-hulls
items.statement: Every smooth variety X over a perfect field k satisfies MS(X): if N ⊆ M are F^n-isocrystals with M †-extendable of constant slopes, then S_1(N) = S_1(N̄).

items.name: Theorem 4.4.12 (Theorem 1.1.1): the parabolicity conjecture
items.statement: Let X be smooth geometrically connected over a perfect field with a perfect point η and M† an overconvergent F^n-isocrystal with constant slopes. Then G(M, η) ⊆ G(M†, η) is the stabiliser of the slope filtration of M_η; if M† is semisimple, G(M, η) is a parabolic subgroup of G(M†, η).

items.name: Arithmetic monodromy groups over a finite field
items.statement: Over F_{p^n} with a rational point x, G(M, Φ_M, x) and G(M†, Φ†_M, x) are the automorphism groups of ω_x on ⟨M, Φ_M⟩ and ⟨M†, Φ†_M⟩, fitting into exact sequences with the geometric groups G(M, x), G(M†, x) and the constant quotients ([AD22, Prop. 2.2.4]).

items.name: Theorem 5.1.2 and Proposition 5.1.3: parabolicity over finite fields
items.statement: Let X be smooth connected over F_{p^n} with a rational point x, G := G(M†, Φ†_M, x) and H := G(M, Φ_M, x). If (M, Φ_M) has constant slopes, then H = P_G(λ), and H is a parabolic subgroup of G when (M†, Φ†_M) is semi-simple (Theorem 5.1.2). For every overconvergent F^n-isocrystal, possibly with non-constant slopes, π_0(H) = π_0(G), and G(M, Φ_M, x)^cst → G(M†, Φ†_M, x)^cst is an isomorphism (Proposition 5.1.3).

items.name: Proposition 5.1.4 and Corollary 5.1.5: the graded pieces and Cartan subgroups
items.statement: With (N, Φ_N) = Gr^S_•(M, Φ_M), G(N, Φ_N, x) = Z_G(λ), and G(N, Φ_N, x)° contains a Cartan subgroup of G(M†, Φ†_M, x)°.

items.name: Reductivity and twist classes of monodromy groups (D'Addezio)
items.statement: For pure overconvergent F-isocrystals over a finite field the geometric monodromy group G(M†, x) is reductive ([D'Ad20, Cor. 3.5.2(ii)]); after a finite extension G(M†, Φ†_M) is connected ([D'Ad20, Prop. 3.3.4]), and the rank of the group of twist classes equals the dimension of the centre ([D'Ad20, Cor. 3.4.8]).
items.locator: Proofs of Theorems 5.1.6 and 5.2.2, pp. 25–26 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Theorem 5.1.6 (Theorem 1.1.2): semisimplicity for abelian schemes
items.statement: Let X be smooth over a finite field and f : A → X an abelian scheme with constant slopes. Then Gr^S_•(R^1f_{crys*}O_{A,crys}) is semisimple; in particular R^1f_{ét*}Q_p is a semisimple lisse Q_p-sheaf.

items.name: Corollary 5.2.1: maximal-slope isoclinic subobjects are †-extendable
items.statement: For a †-extendable F^n-isocrystal over smooth X, every isoclinic subobject of maximal slope is †-extendable.

items.name: Albert types and the Cadoret–Tamagawa criterion
items.statement: Albert's classification of endomorphism algebras of simple abelian varieties (types I–IV); for geometrically simple A, a factor of type IV follows once the centre of G(M†, Φ†_M)° has dimension ≥ 2 ([CT20, Lem. 10.5]).
items.locator: Theorem 5.2.2 and its proof, p. 26 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Theorem 5.2.2 (Theorem 1.1.3): finiteness of separable p-power torsion
items.statement: Let E be finitely generated over F_p and A an abelian variety over E. Then A(E^sep)[p^∞] is finite if End(A) ⊗ Q_p is a division algebra, or if End(A) ⊗ Q has no factor of Albert type IV.

items.name: Corollary 5.3.1 (Corollary 1.1.4): Kedlaya's conjecture
items.statement: Over smooth connected X over a perfect field, two irreducible overconvergent F^n-isocrystals with constant slopes whose minimal-slope parts (S_1(M_i), Φ|) are isomorphic are isomorphic.

items.name: Corollary 5.3.2: minimal-slope parts of irreducibles are irreducible
items.statement: If (M†, Φ†_M) is an irreducible overconvergent F^n-isocrystal with constant slopes then (S_1(M), Φ_M|) is irreducible.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.3 (Theorem 1.1.5): strong multiplicity one by minimal-slope Hecke eigenvalues
items.statement: Let X be a smooth connected curve over a finite field, A its adeles and r ≥ 1. The isomorphism class of a Q̄_p-linear cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_r(A) is determined by its Hecke eigenvalues of minimal slope at all but finitely many closed points.

items.name: Definition 5.4.1 and Corollary 5.4.2: the PBS filtration
items.statement: A †-extendable F^n-isocrystal is PBS if on every connected open the isoclinic subobjects have minimal generic slope (dual to Tsuzuki's PBQ). Over a smooth connected variety over a perfect field, every †-extendable M has a unique filtration by †-extendable subobjects with PBS graded pieces of minimal generic slopes t_1 > ··· > t_r (extending [Tsu23, Thm. 3.27]).

items.name: Definition 5.4.3 and Corollary 5.4.4: minimal †-compactifications
items.statement: A †-compactification of (N, Φ_N) is a †-extendable M with ι : N ↪ M and N̄ = M; if N is isoclinic and embeds into a †-extendable F^n-isocrystal, it has a minimal (weakly final) †-compactification.

items.name: Frobenius acts semi-simply on the cohomology of an abelian variety over a finite field
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over F_q, the q-Frobenius π_A lies in the centre of the semisimple Q-algebra End⁰(A), so Q[π_A] is a product of number fields and π_A acts semi-simply on H^1_crys(A/W(F_q)) ⊗ Q and on V_ℓA for ℓ ≠ p.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.1.6, p. 25 (arXiv v4: "the action of the p^n-th power Frobenius on the crystalline cohomology groups of A_x is semi-simple (this Frobenius is in the centre of End(A_x))"); used again in the proof of Theorem 5.2.2, p. 26

routes.reason: RD.1 owns Frobenius slope filtrations, RD.2 unipotent local monodromy with its logarithmic extensions, and RD.3 overconvergent isocrystals with their restriction to convergent ones. The paper's cited foundations — generic slope filtrations, Kedlaya's full faithfulness at the generic point and on dense opens, de Jong's reverse filtration, Crew's unit-root correspondence, docility and semistable reduction, Étesse's overconvergence of R^1f_crys — are theorems of those layers, as PAPER-TSUZUKI-23's accepted route 1, which spans RD.0–RD.6, routes the same inputs to that roadmap. Review (REV-PAPER-DADDEZIO-23): RD.3 is unrelated to RD.1 and RD.2 in the atlas, so items that need both belong in RD.5, the first stage downstream of RD.1, RD.2 and RD.3, which already plans "the relative local-monodromy input used in Kedlaya's proof, then devissage and alterations/descent": Kedlaya's full faithfulness (items 9 and 10, which use RD.1's slope filtration with RD.3), docility and semistable reduction (items 13 and 14, which use RD.2 with RD.3). Two links are needed, neither closing a cycle: CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 → RD.3 for Étesse's theorem (item 15) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0 → RD.3 for the slope filtration after removing a divisor (item 8).

R07.2 owns Dieudonné theory over perfect fields; the crystalline Dieudonné module of A[p^∞] over a smooth base (BBM) and de Jong's full faithfulness for Barsotti–Tate groups over function fields continue that layer to families. Review: the crystalline Dieudonné module over a smooth base (item 16) uses relative crystalline cohomology with Frobenius and base change (CrystallineCohomology CR.3), which is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of R07.2; the link CR.3 → R07.2 is needed and closes no cycle. De Jong's theorem (item 17) extends R07.2 beyond perfect fields and depends on item 16. For the orchestrator: CR.7's description exports crystals "to R07's Dieudonne crystal", but R07.2 → CR.7 is an atlas edge, so the two disagree about where the Dieudonné crystal is built.

FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 plans "a function-field Chebotarev statement retaining the congruence restriction on degrees imposed by constants", and the paper uses Chebotarev only for a smooth curve over a finite field (proof of Theorem 5.3.3). As corrected in review (REV-PAPER-DADDEZIO-23), the route was sent to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4, which is number-field only; the precedent it cited, PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16's AN.4 route, was rejected by its review for the same reason.

routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: the Langlands correspondence for isocrystals and crystalline companions
routes.brief: This route coalesces with the GlobalShtukasPartIICrystallineCompanions candidate proposed by PAPER-ABE-18 (same id, title, parent and area) and keeps its brief. PAPER-DADDEZIO-23 consumes Abe's Theorem 4.2.2 exactly as that brief states it: every Q̄_p-linear cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_r(A) over a function field corresponds to an irreducible overconvergent F-isocrystal on a dense open with matching Frobenius and Hecke eigenvalues. It adds no target; its consumer is the strong multiplicity one theorem by minimal-slope Hecke eigenvalues (PAPER-DADDEZIO-23, Theorem 5.3.3), which lives in PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIMonodromyGroups and imports the correspondence from here.

routes.title: P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights, Part II: PBQ filtrations and minimal slopes
routes.brief: This route coalesces with PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIMinimalSlope as proposed by PAPER-TSUZUKI-23 (same id, title, parent and area) and keeps its brief. D'Addezio (Ann. of Math. 198 (2023)) adds a second proof of the curve case of the minimal slope property: the †-hull N̄ of a sub-F^n-isocrystal (Definition 4.1.1), the property MS (Notation 4.1.2) and its reductions to n = 1, isoclinic subobjects, dense opens and finite étale Galois covers (Lemmas 4.1.4–4.1.8); the generic statement S_1(N) = S_1(N̄) over E (Proposition 4.2.2) via the dual construction of the hull (Lemma 4.2.4), de Jong's reverse slope filtration and Lemma 4.2.7; the integral models A_n, B_n, B̃_n and Lemmas 4.2.10–4.2.11; the comparison of hulls with the generic point (Proposition 4.2.12, whose printed proof needs the repair noted in PAPER-DADDEZIO-23/E5, or Tsuzuki's route); and Theorem 4.2.13, MS for smooth curves over a perfect field, reduced to A^1 by Kedlaya's étale covers. The Abe–Esnault Lefschetz full-faithfulness theorem for docile isocrystals (AE19, Cor. 2.4) is recorded here next to Tsuzuki's Abe–Esnault curve input. The higher-dimensional MS theorem of D'Addezio belongs to PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIMonodromyGroups, which imports this roadmap; nothing here may import it back. Import the parent's slope filtrations (RD.1), local monodromy (RD.2) and overconvergent coefficient categories (RD.3).
routes.reason: The curve case of MS and its generic-point proof are exactly the minimal-slope theory that PAPER-TSUZUKI-23's Part II owns; a second roadmap for the same theorem would duplicate it.

routes.title: P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights, Part II: monodromy groups of F-isocrystals and the parabolicity conjecture
routes.brief: Extend P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology) by the Tannakian monodromy theory of F-isocrystals, following D'Addezio, Parabolicity conjecture of F-isocrystals (Ann. of Math. 198 (2023), 619–656). Final theorems, as the paper states them: Theorem 4.4.12 (X smooth geometrically connected over a perfect field k with a perfect point η; for every overconvergent F^n-isocrystal M† over X with constant slopes, G(M, η) ⊆ G(M†, η) is the stabiliser of the slope filtration of M_η, and it is a parabolic subgroup when M† is semi-simple); Theorem 4.1.3 (every smooth variety over a perfect field satisfies MS); Theorem 4.4.3 (for Y ⊆ P^d_{k^alg} smooth connected projective of dimension ≥ 2, D a simple normal crossing divisor and M† docile along D on X = Y ∖ D, there is a smooth connected curve C ⊆ X meeting the dense open where the slopes of M† are constant with ⟨M†⟩ → ⟨M†|_C⟩ an equivalence); Theorem 5.1.6 (for X smooth over F_{p^n} and an abelian scheme A → X with constant slopes, Gr^S of R^1f_crys*O_{A,crys} is semi-simple, and R^1f_ét*Q_p is a semi-simple lisse Q_p-sheaf); Theorem 5.2.2 (for an abelian variety A over a finitely generated field E/F_p, A(E^sep)[p^∞] is finite if End(A) ⊗ Q_p is a division algebra, or if End(A) ⊗ Q has no factor of Albert type IV); Corollary 5.3.1 (Kedlaya's conjecture: two irreducible overconvergent F^n-isocrystals with constant slopes over a smooth connected variety over a perfect field are isomorphic if their minimal-slope parts S_1 are); Theorem 5.3.3 (for a smooth connected curve X over a finite field, a Q_p-linear cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_r(A) is determined by its Hecke eigenvalues of minimal slope at all but finitely many closed points); Corollaries 5.4.2 and 5.4.4 (the PBS filtration; minimal †-compactifications of isoclinic F^n-isocrystals that embed in a †-extendable one). Layers: (1) Crew's monodromy groups, observable functors and scalar extension; (2) isocrystals with punctual Q_p^ur-structure, Dieudonné–Manin structures, Λ_η, the exact sequences of Proposition 3.2.8 and the base change G(M, η) = G(M, V_M, η) ⊗ K; (3) the slope quasi-cocharacter, Saavedra's P_G(λ), Chevalley's theorem and Propositions 4.3.2–4.3.5; (4) the Lefschetz theorem through Lemmas 4.4.5–4.4.7, Corollary 4.4.8 and a Bertini theorem with tangency conditions; (5) MS in all dimensions and parabolicity; (6) the applications over finite and finitely generated fields. Import MS for curves and the Abe–Esnault Lefschetz theorem from PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIMinimalSlope; slope filtrations, full faithfulness, docility and semistable reduction from RD.1–RD.3; Dieudonné–Manin from VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0; Tannaka groups from MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.6; parabolic subgroups from the Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7; crystalline Dieudonné theory from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2; weights of abelian varieties from WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.2; Chebotarev for curves over finite fields from FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5; Abe's correspondence from GlobalShtukasPartIICrystallineCompanions. Review (REV-PAPER-DADDEZIO-23): KloostermanSheavesAndBesselIsocrystals (PAPER-XU-ZHU-22, accepted route 3) defines monodromy groups of Bessel F-isocrystals and should import Crew's monodromy groups from this Part II. Lemma 4.4.7 is proved and used only for cyclic quotients of prime order (E13). The Frobenius-semisimplicity input of Theorem 5.1.6 (item 71) is a corollary of the semisimple endomorphism algebra of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6.
routes.reason: No layer or proposal plans Crew's monodromy groups of F-isocrystals or their parabolicity; the ℓ-adic monodromy continuations (GlobalShtukasPartIICompanions) treat lisse sheaves. The theory builds on the parent's coefficient categories and on the minimal-slope Part II, and the higher-dimensional MS theorem must sit here rather than there, because its proof uses the monodromy groups and the Lefschetz theorem (a roadmap cycle otherwise). Review: the brief now states the final theorems with their hypotheses. Remark 3.1.7 (the former item 38), an unproved aside that nothing later uses, is no longer an item, and item 71 is added.
